text:
Maya: Heads-up — Azure Marketplace applied promo seat credits to the wrong subscription for AcmeCorp. Invoice IN-44521 shows a -$12,000 credit on subscription sub-prod-001 but the usage tied to sub-prod-002. Can someone check allocation rules?
Owen: Ugh. Do we have the invoice PDF or billing CSV?
Maya: Uploaded the CSV to the billing bucket: s3://redwood-billing/marketplace/acme/IN-44521.csv. Quick excerpt: ```subscription_id,partner_id,sku,credits
sub-prod-001,partner-az-90,seat:monthly,-12000
sub-prod-002,partner-az-90,seat:monthly,0```
Priya: Looking now. On initial glance the partner mapping for sub-prod-002 seems to have changed during the month (partner_id rotated). Marketplace exports use subscription-level partner_id for credit routing. If partner_id on the exported row matched sub-prod-001, credit would go there.
Liam: cc @billing-bot — can we pull the raw marketplace report for the 2026-03 billing window and show the subscription->partner mapping history?
billing-bot: Automated note: Marketplace report for Mar 2026 (report_id: MP-2026-03-ACME) available at https://storage.redwood/marketplace/MP-2026-03-ACME.csv
Priya: I grepped the report — looks like on 2026-03-10 subscription sub-prod-002 was updated by partner sync to partner-az-91, then reverted on 2026-03-18 to partner-az-90. The export run happened on 2026-03-17 so the row captured partner-az-91 for sub-prod-002, which is why credits landed on sub-prod-001 (the only other subscription still marked partner-az-90).
Owen: So it's a timing issue between partner sync and export snapshot. Do we have a recon rule to aggregate credits by customer when partner mapping flips mid-window?
Priya: Not currently — credits are allocated at subscription granularity exactly as the report rows. We can file a retroactive reallocation request with Azure marketplace but we'll need a clear audit trail.
Maya: What docs/data do they need for reallocation? I can assemble.
Liam: Typically Azure needs invoice id, the original marketplace report row, proof of intended subscription mapping (customer support ticket or onboarding doc), and a signed reclassification form. It can take 4-6 weeks.
Owen: Can we issue an internal credit to sub-prod-002 to fix the customer's billing now, then pursue marketplace reallocation later? That might preserve ACV recognition for the CS team.
Priya: Internal credit is OK but we need approval from revenue ops. Also want to ensure we don't double-credit if marketplace approves. We should tag this as tentative until resolution.
Maya: I'll prepare a one-pager for RevOps with: invoice id, marketplace report excerpt, subscription change history, requested reallocation amount ($12,000), and suggested interim internal credit.
Owen: I'll ping RevOps. @Liam can you draft the reclassification request template we send to Azure (so Maya can attach it)?
Liam: Yep. I'll reuse last quarter's template and update the fields. ETA EOD today.
Maya: Thanks — will loop in the customer success lead so AcmeCorp sees progress. @Priya can you also add the partner sync job run timestamps and logs to the packet?
Priya: On it. Posting the sync log snippet here: ```2026-03-10T03:22:11Z sub-prod-002 partner set: partner-az-91 by sync-job-7
2026-03-18T04:05:09Z sub-prod-002 partner set: partner-az-90 by sync-job-7```
billing-bot: Note saved to case FIN-ACME-2026-03 (attachments: IN-44521.csv, MP-2026-03-ACME.csv, sync-log.txt)
Maya: Ok plan: 1) Owen to request internal interim credit once RevOps approves. 2) Liam to prepare Azure reclassification request. 3) Priya to attach sync logs and marketplace snapshots. 4) Maya to notify CS and customer. If anyone has objections speak now. :thumbsup:
Owen: +1
Priya: +1
Liam: +1
Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll update this thread after RevOps reply.
